original_query: SELECT t4.NAME FROM (SELECT NAME, DEPTNO, DEPTNO - 10 AS DEPTNOMINUS FROM DEPT) AS t4 INNER JOIN (SELECT DEPTNO, SAL + 1 AS f9 FROM EMP GROUP BY DEPTNO, SAL + 1) AS t6 ON t4.DEPTNOMINUS = t6.f9 AND t4.DEPTNO = t6.DEPTNO
rewritten_query:
SELECT d.NAME
FROM DEPT d
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM EMP e
    WHERE e.DEPTNO = d.DEPTNO
      AND e.SAL = d.DEPTNO - 11
);

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the derived table with GROUP BY over the 45M-row EMP table and the subsequent INNER JOIN with an EXISTS semi-join. Since the grouped derived table can match each DEPT row at most once, EXISTS is semantically equivalent and avoids the expensive HashAggregate/FinalizeAggregate over EMP entirely.
Flatten both derived tables (t4 from DEPT, t6 from EMP) into the main query. The projections (DEPTNOMINUS, f9) add no value and prevent predicate pushdown.
Rewrite the non-sargable predicate `e.SAL + 1 = d.DEPTNO - 10` as the equivalent `e.SAL = d.DEPTNO - 11`, isolating the bare column on the EMP side so an index on EMP(DEPTNO, SAL) can be used.

The semi-join allows the optimizer to stop scanning EMP as soon as one match per DEPT row is found (with an index), or to use a cheaper hash semi-join (one scan of each table) without aggregation. Recommend a composite index `EMP(DEPTNO, SAL)` as a physical optimization.
